# Database Engine (DBEngine) API & Driver Contract Specification

Low-level database persistence and query layer executing SQL statements, connection pooling, batch
inserts/upserts, parallel table commits, declarative query specifications, and DDL schema/view management for `TableEngine`, `ChangeSet`, and `webapp`.

## SQL Habit to API

First stop for a `db_engine` call: the generated signature list `db_engine/API_SURFACE.md` (cache stores: `cache_engine/API_SURFACE.md`). All names below are importable from `db_engine` unless a module is given; `db` is a `BaseDBEngine` (`G.DB`), `Where` forms and `Expr` classes are in section 2.6.

| SQL / driver habit | API |
|---|---|
| `INSERT IGNORE` | `db.insert_rows(table, cols, rows, on_conflict="ignore")` |
| `ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE col = VALUES(col)` | `db.insert_rows(..., on_conflict="update", update_columns=[...])` |
| Upsert with expressions (`n = n + 1`, `IF(VALUES(x) > x, ...)`) | `db.insert_rows(..., on_conflict="update", update_exprs={"n": add("n", 1), "x": Case([(where, value)], otherwise)})`; `Incoming("col")` is the offered value, a bare column name the stored value |
| `REPLACE INTO` | `db.insert_rows(..., on_conflict="replace")` |
| `INSERT ... SELECT` | `db.copy_rows(table, cols, Select(...), on_conflict="error"\|"ignore")` |
| `DELETE ... WHERE ... LIMIT n` | `db.delete_rows(table, where, limit=n)`; `all_rows=True` for a whole table |
| Multi-table `DELETE` / `DELETE ... WHERE x IN (SELECT ...)` | `db.delete_rows(table, [in_select("col", Select(...))])`; subquery terms (`in_select`, `exists_select`, `NotExists`, `Exists`) go in a list `Where` |
| `UPDATE ... SET c = CASE WHEN ... END` / `IF(...)` | `db.update_rows(table, {"c": Case([(where, value)], otherwise)}, where)`; `Inc(1)`, `Col("other")` and any `Expr` read the stored row |
| `information_schema.TABLES` | `db.table_exists(name)`, `db.existing_tables(names, include_views=)`, `db.table_stats(names)` |
| `information_schema.COLUMNS` | `db.column_exists(table, col)`, `db.column_info(table, col)`, `db.add_column(table, col, ColumnSpec(...))` |
| `information_schema.STATISTICS` / `SHOW INDEX` | `db.index_names(table)`, `db.index_exists(name, table)`, `db.create_index(...)` |
| `SHOW TABLES` / `SHOW VARIABLES` | `db.existing_tables(names)`; `db.server_variable(name)` |
| `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW` | `db.create_view(name, Select(...))`; registered views in `db_engine/views.py`, created by `db.ensure_views()` |
| `CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE` / anti-join scratch tables | `with db.new_checkpoint_pairs(commit_id, prev_commit_id) as pairs:`; otherwise `db.copy_rows` into a regular `Table` and `db.drop_table` |
| `LIKE '%x%'` with escaping | `{"col": like(text, "prefix"\|"suffix"\|"contains"\|"exact", ci=False)}` (escapes `% _ \`) |
| `WHERE id IN (...)` with thousands of values | `{"id": values}` (a list); oversize lists are chunked by `select_rows`, `update_rows` and `delete_rows`; `db.select_in(table, col_idx, values)` |
| `GROUP BY ... HAVING` | `db.aggregate(source, {"n": Agg("COUNT", "*")}, where, group_by=[...], having=Pred(Agg("COUNT"), ge(2)))` or `Select(group_by=, having=)` |
| `CONCAT`, `LENGTH`, `SUBSTR`/`LEFT`, `COALESCE`, `NULLIF`, `HEX`, `a + b` | `Concat`, `Length`, `Substr`, `Coalesce`, `NullIf`, `Hex`, `add` / `sub` / `mul` |
| `col IS NULL` / `IS NOT NULL` | `{"col": None}` / `is_null()` / `not_null()` |
| `COUNT(*)`, `EXISTS`, `MAX(col)` | `db.count_rows`, `db.row_exists`, `db.max_value` / `db.min_value` |
| `commit()` / `rollback()` / `START TRANSACTION` | `with db.transaction():` (commit on exit, rollback on error) |
| `cursor.execute(...)` + `fetchall()` / `fetchone()` | `db.select_rows`, `db.select_one`, `db.select_values`, `db.select_value`; streaming: `db.iter_rows` |
| `cursor.lastrowid`, `SELECT ... ; INSERT` for a surrogate id | `db.get_or_insert_id(table, key, values)`, `db.reserve_id_block(table, n)` |
| Webapp read of the database | `with get_reader() as reader:` (`webapp/backend/database/pool.py`), a `ReadSession` with the `ReadIntents` methods |
| Local rebuildable cache file (`sqlite3.connect(...)`) | `cache_engine.get_cache_engine().open(namespace, name, [StoreSpec(...)])` (`cache_engine/CACHE_API.md`) |
| Reading or writing a foreign SQLite file (public-inbox) | `db_engine.open_foreign_sqlite(path)` / `db_engine.create_foreign_sqlite(path)` |
| `except mysql.connector.Error` / error numbers (1062, 1146, 1153, 2013) | `DuplicateKeyError`, `MissingTableError`, `PacketTooLargeError`, `ConnectionLostError` (all `DBError`, `db_engine/errors.py`) |

## 1. Architectural Architecture & Interface Overview

Any database backend assigned to `G.DB` or passed to `TableEngine.start()` must implement the abstract
contract defined in [`BaseDBEngine`](db_engine/base.py).

### Encapsulation & Query Authority Contract

`db_engine` is the single authoritative subsystem for interacting with the database across the entire project. All SQL execution, DDL/schema migrations, view declarations, transactions, batch operations, connection pooling, and sequence coordination must reside inside `db_engine/` and adhere to `BaseDBEngine`.

Outside `db_engine/` (`main.py`, `core/`, `parser/`, `webapp/`, `table_engine/`, `cache_engine/`) there is no SQL text, no driver import (`mysql.connector`, `pymysql`, `sqlite3`), no connection or cursor handle (`cnx`, `cursor()`), no `execute*()` / `query*()` call, and no check of the backend type (`isinstance(db, MockDB)`, `hasattr(db, "query")`). The raw SQL entry points are the driver-private `_raw_cursor`, `_raw_query*`, `_raw_execute*` and `_raw_delete`, used only by `db_engine/` internals (catalog defaults, DDL, temp-table helpers) and driver unit tests; read sessions expose none. Callers use query specs (`db_engine/spec.py`) through the spec methods and the named intent methods of `BaseDBEngine` / `ReadSession`; a pattern none of them covers becomes a new method in `db_engine/` implemented once in `db_engine/base.py` or `db_engine/read_intents.py` over specs. Backend-conditional behaviour lives only in `db_engine/` (as a method, option or capability flag) and in `cache_engine/` for local caches; the webapp reads through `get_reader()`, local caches go through `cache_engine/`, and foreign SQLite files through `db_engine.open_foreign_sqlite()`. `tests/test_db_boundary.py` enforces these rules by an AST scan of every `.py` file outside `db_engine/` (an allowlist of engine-internals tests and `core/TableHandling.py` is itself checked for stale entries).

### Neutral Errors (`db_engine/errors.py`)

Callers catch only these classes; each driver maps its native errors at its boundary with
`raise Neutral(...) from native_error` (the original stays on `__cause__`).

| Class | Also a | Raised for |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `DBError` | `Exception` | Base of every class below. |
| `UnsupportedOperation` | `NotImplementedError` | The backend lacks the operation (raw SQL on `MockDB`, a base-class method a driver does not implement). The message names the replacement API and the section of this document. |
| `SpecError` | `ValueError` | A specification is malformed: mixed condition / IN list, mapping as a condition value, `lt(None)`-style NULL comparison, unknown alias, assignments that read each other. The message names the fix and this document's section. |
| `DuplicateKeyError` | `ValueError` | Primary-key / unique violation (`insert()` and `insert_rows(on_conflict="error")`; MariaDB errno 1062). |
| `MissingTableError` | `LookupError` | Unknown table or view (MariaDB errno 1146 / 1051; `SQLiteDB` / `MockDB` for "no such table" (a `MockDB` name that was dropped, or is neither a `core/DBLayout.py` table, a `Table` the call passed nor a registry view); `SQLiteStore` / `ForeignReader` for "no such table"). `sqlite_store.MissingTableError` subclasses it. |
| `ConnectionLostError` | `ConnectionError` | Connection lost, refused or not obtainable (errno 2002/2003/2006/2013/2055/1927, `InterfaceError`, pool exhaustion, an `OperationalError` without a statement-level number). |
| `PacketTooLargeError` | | Statement above the server packet limit (errno 1153/1154, `max_allowed_packet`); batch writers bisect internally first. |
| `ConfigurationError` | | The connection settings are incomplete (`MariaDB` without `DB_USER` / `DB_PASSWORD`, i.e. `database.user` / `database.password`): no default account exists, and the error names the keys to set. |
| `ReadOnlyViolation` | | A write entry point was called on a read-only session (`ReadSession`, `MockReadSession`, a `MariaDB` driver backing a reader); the message points at the writer engine. |

Every error raised by `db_engine` that a caller can fix (`UnsupportedOperation`, `SpecError`, `ReadOnlyViolation`, `PoolConfigError`, `ConfigurationError`, `MissingTableError`) names the replacement API and the section of this document by name, in one or two lines. `tests/test_db_boundary.py` failures carry the same hint per rule.

`translate_mysql_error(exc) -> DBError | None` holds the mapping (errno first, message second, class last; `None` = no
neutral equivalent, the native error propagates). `MariaDB` wraps its public entry points (the private `_raw_*` SQL entry points,
`select*`, `insert*`, `update*`, `delete_rows`, `copy_rows`, `drop_*`, `create_*`, `commit`, `commit_tables_parallel`, ...) with it,
keeping a `failed_table_ids` attribute on the neutral error; `transaction()` translates the errors of its own `SET autocommit` /
`COMMIT` the same way.

### Capability Flags

`BaseDBEngine.capabilities` is a `frozenset[str]`; `has_capability(name)` tests one. Callers branch on a flag, never on
`isinstance(db, MockDB)` or `hasattr(db, ...)`.

| Flag (`CAP_*` constant) | Meaning | MariaDB | MockDB | SQLiteDB |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `persistent` (`CAP_PERSISTENT`) | Data outlives the process; DB-only maintenance steps (layout checks, backfills over stored rows) make sense. | yes | no | file only |
| `server_tuning` (`CAP_SERVER_TUNING`) | `apply_server_tuning()` can change server variables. | yes | no | no |
| `background_commit` (`CAP_BACKGROUND_COMMIT`) | `commit_tables_parallel(dedicated=True)` may run on a writer thread (mirrors `supports_background_commit`). | yes | no | no |
| `concurrent_connections` (`CAP_CONCURRENT_CONNECTIONS`) | Independent connections see one database (parallel workers, reader pool). | yes | no | no |

Other class attributes: `dialect` (`"mariadb"` / `"sqlite"`, the `sql_render` dialect of the engine) and
`default_socket_paths` (local server socket candidates; `MariaDB`: `/run/mysqld/mysqld.sock`,
`/var/run/mysqld/mysqld.sock`, `/tmp/mysql.sock`; empty for socketless engines).

| `Public API listing` | [`API_SURFACE.md`](db_engine/API_SURFACE.md) | Generated signatures + first docstring line of the public API (`python3 .agents/scripts/api_surface.py --write`). |

| `MockDB` | [`mock_db.py`](db_engine/mock_db.py) | `SQLiteDB` subclass over an in-memory SQLite database (one per instance, or one shared by every `use_global=True` instance) for isolated, fast tests without a server (§2.15 "MockDB"). | `SQLiteDB` | [`sqlite_db.py`](db_engine/sqlite_db.py) | `BaseDBEngine` over a SQLite file or `:memory:` database (`database.engine: "sqlite"`): schema DDL rendered from the neutral `DBLayout` column specs, the spec renderers with `dialect="sqlite"`, thread-safe single connection per instance (`RLock`, WAL for files), `transaction()`, a `mode=ro` / `query_only` `SQLiteReadSession` from `reader()`, and the full TableEngine, spec, catalog and pipeline-intent surface (see "SQLiteDB" below). |
| `SQLiteStore` | [`sqlite_store.py`](db_engine/sqlite_store.py) | Standalone embedded SQLite store (not a `BaseDBEngine` driver, not selectable through `get_db_engine`) with WAL mode, thread-safe connection caching, schema reflection, key-value metadata store, declarative spec reads, and batch inserts. |
| `Errors` | [`errors.py`](db_engine/errors.py) | Neutral exception hierarchy exported from `db_engine` (see "Neutral Errors" below): `DBError`, `UnsupportedOperation`, `DuplicateKeyError`, `MissingTableError`, `ConnectionLostError`, `PacketTooLargeError`, `ReadOnlyViolation`. |
| `Foreign reader` | [`foreign.py`](db_engine/foreign.py) | `open_foreign_sqlite(path)` -> `ForeignReader`: read-only spec reads over a SQLite file written by another program (§2.14). |
| `Declarative Specs` | [`spec.py`](db_engine/spec.py) | Pure data types and condition helpers (`Cond`, `Join`, `Agg`, `Const`, `Select`, `AnyOf`, `Exists`, `InSelect`, expressions, `ColumnSpec`, etc.) enabling typed, SQL-free query formulation. |
| `SQL Renderer` | [`sql_render.py`](db_engine/sql_render.py) | Multi-dialect SQL compiler rendering declarative query specs to parameterized SQL for `mariadb` and `sqlite`. |
| `Read intents` | [`read_intents.py`](db_engine/read_intents.py) | `ReadIntents` mixin: domain read methods implemented once over query specs and inherited by `ReadSession`, `MockReadSession`, `SQLiteReadSession` (§2.12). |
| `Symbol rows` | [`symbol_rows.py`](db_engine/symbol_rows.py) | Key-first symbol reference / definition readers (`symbol_refs_of_targets`, `symbol_def_blobs_of_targets`; `in_select` subquery on `m_blob_symbol`) shared by every backend. |
| `View Registry` | [`views.py`](db_engine/views.py) | Canonical dependency-ordered view definitions registry (`VIEW_DEFINITIONS`, `ORDERED_VIEW_NAMES`, `extract_select_sql`). |
| `ReadSession` | [`pool.py`](db_engine/pool.py) | Read-only connection wrapper (`ReadAPI`) providing dictionary-oriented spec reads and domain intent methods for `webapp/`. |

## 2. Core Method Specifications

### 2.1. Lifecycle, Session & Health
- **`__init__() -> None`**
  - Connects to database via Unix domain socket (`DB_SOCKET` / `MYSQL_UNIX_PORT`, e.g.
    `/run/mysqld/mysqld.sock`) when local and non-tunneled, or falls back to TCP socket (`DB_HOST`,
    `DB_PORT`). The connection runs with `autocommit` on and `FOUND_ROWS`. `_init_session()` sets the session's
    `sql_mode = 'NO_AUTO_VALUE_ON_ZERO'`, `foreign_key_checks = 0`, `unique_checks = 0`, `wait_timeout` /
    `interactive_timeout` 28800 s and `net_read_timeout` / `net_write_timeout` 3600 s in one combined
    `SET SESSION` statement (with a `sql_mode` fallback). Credentials come from `DB_USER` / `DB_PASSWORD` only; without them the connection raises `ConfigurationError` (no default account).
- **`__enter__() -> Self` & `__exit__(...) -> None`**
  - Context manager lifecycle; rolls back pending transaction on unhandled exception.
- **`close() -> None`**
  - Safely releases cursor and database connection socket handles.
- **`_raw_cursor(dictionary: bool = False) -> Any`** *(driver-private)*
  - Leases a fresh driver cursor (`MariaDB`: after `check_if_connected()`). The driver's internal shared cursor is the private attribute `_cur`. `MockDB` raises `UnsupportedOperation`. Together with `_raw_query`, `_raw_query_one`, `_raw_query_iter`, `_raw_execute`, `_raw_executemany` and `_raw_delete` this is the raw-SQL surface that only `db_engine/` internals (catalog defaults, DDL, temp-table helpers) and driver-level unit tests use; consumers outside `db_engine/` never call it (`tests/test_db_boundary.py`).
- **`probe_connection(cfg: Mapping[str, Any]) -> ProbeResult`** *(classmethod, never raises)*
  - Tries to connect with a `database` config section and returns `ProbeResult(ok, version, latency_ms, error, target)`.
    `MariaDB` needs `user` and `database`; honors `host`, `port`, `password`, `ssl_disabled`, `timeout` (default 3 s) and
    `unix_socket` (`"auto"` probes `default_socket_paths` for a local host, `"off"`/`"none"`/`"disabled"`/`"false"` forces TCP, a
    path is used when it exists), falls back to TCP `host:port` when the socket connection fails and a host is set, runs
    `SELECT 1` and reports the server version. `target` names the socket or `host:port` used. SSH-tunnel orchestration is
    the caller's job: it resolves the forwarded `host`/`port` first. `MockDB` is always ok; the base class reports
    "not implemented".
- **`reader()`, `warm_up()`, `shutdown()`** *(class-level lifecycle for the webapp)*
  - `Engine.reader()` returns a context manager yielding a read-only `ReadSession` (callable on the class or an instance;
    `MariaDB`: a pooled session, `MockDB`: a `MockReadSession` (the `SQLiteReadSession`) over the shared in-memory database). `Engine.warm_up()` builds the shared reader pool
    and starts the configured SSH tunnel (`MariaDB`: the private connection pool of `db_engine/pool.py`); `Engine.shutdown()` closes it. Base and
    `MockDB` implement both as no-ops. `webapp/backend/app.py` calls them on the class resolved from `database.engine`.
- **`check_if_connected() -> None`** *(no-op on the base class, MockDB and SQLiteDB)*
  - A connection that completed a statement within `IDLE_PING_S` (30 s) is used without any round trip; an idle
    one is checked with one `ping()`. A missing or dead connection is replaced (`_reconnect()`: new connection,
    new cursor, `_init_session()`, up to 3 attempts, then `ConnectionLostError`), so a new session always has
    `sql_mode` and the disabled checks. A forked child drops the connection it inherited without closing it (that
    would end the parent's session) and opens its own.
  - Inside `transaction()` it checks nothing: a dead connection makes the next statement fail, the server has
    already rolled the transaction back, and the caller retries all of it.
  - Reads (`select`, `select_in`, `select_preload`, `table_size`, `get_next_id`, `view_select*`, `test_tables`,
    `_raw_query*`, so every spec read) run through `_read()`: outside `transaction()` a read whose connection was
    lost (errno 2006 / 2013 / 2055, `InterfaceError`, socket errors) reconnects and runs once more. Writes
    outside a transaction keep their per-chunk retry (`insert()`, `update()`, `insert_rows()`). Outside
    `transaction()` the driver relies on the connection's autocommit: no statement reads `@@autocommit` and no
    no-op `COMMIT` follows a write; `commit()` commits only inside `transaction()`.
- **`transaction() -> ContextManager[Self]`**
  - `BaseDBEngine` default yields without transactional guarantees; `SQLiteDB` and `MockDB` run the block as one SQLite transaction that rolls back when it raises. `MariaDB` runs the block's `insert()` / `update()` calls as one transaction (`autocommit` off, one `COMMIT` on exit,
    `ROLLBACK` on error). Inside it `insert()` / `update()` neither commit per call nor reconnect and retry
    per chunk, so a table is written completely or not at all and can be retried as a whole.
    `reserve_id_block()` commits on its own and raises `UnsupportedOperation` inside it (`MariaDB`, `SQLiteDB`, `MockDB`).
- **`apply_server_tuning(settings: dict[str, Any] | None = None, *, tunnel_active: bool | None = None, mem_max_gb: float = 0.0) -> list[str]`**
  - `BaseDBEngine` and `MockDB` return no notes; `MariaDB` raises global server variables with `SET GLOBAL` (needs SUPER; lasts until the server restarts) and
    returns one note per change or failure. With `tunnel_active` given (`False` = the server is local, `True` = reached
    through an SSH tunnel; `None` skips this logic) a local server's `innodb_buffer_pool_size` is capped at a quarter of
    the machine's RAM rounded down to 128 MB, and a `memory guard ...` note is appended when `mem_max_gb` GB plus the
    pool the server really runs with (read back with `server_variable()`) exceed the RAM. `tuning_note_is_warning(note)`
    (exported) classifies a note as warning-worthy (`capped at`, `kept`, `not available`, `memory guard`). Sizes may carry a K/M/G/T suffix (`parse_server_setting()`);
    `innodb_buffer_pool_size`, `innodb_log_file_size`, `innodb_io_capacity(_max)` are never lowered, and
    `innodb_io_capacity_max` goes first. Each value is read back: a server that caps it (e.g.
    `innodb_buffer_pool_size` beyond `innodb_buffer_pool_size_max`, which MariaDB 10.11 fixes at startup) is
    reported as `capped at ...` with the restart hint. If the user lacks the privilege (`errno 1227`, e.g. a
    remote server reached over the SSH tunnel), the remaining variables are not tried and a single `server
    tuning skipped: ...` note is returned, which `main.py` logs at INFO level instead of one warning per
    variable.

### 2.2. Sequence Tracking & Single-Row CRUD
- **`get_next_id(table: Table) -> int`**
  - Queries `COALESCE(MAX(pk), 0) + 1` on table primary key. Returns 1 if table is empty.
- **`reserve_id_block(table: Table, block_size: int, commit_id: int = 0) -> tuple[int, int]`**
  - Atomically reserves a block of primary key IDs `[start_id, end_id]` via `m_table_sequence` for distributed
    multi-computer coordination and logs the range in `m_ingest_id_range`. Falls back to `get_next_id()` when
    sequence table or multi-computer mode is unavailable.
  - `MariaDB`: reads the floor `COALESCE(MAX(pk), 0) + 1` with a plain consistent read (no locks, so it never waits
    for a commit appending to the same table), then in one transaction upserts it
    (`next_id = GREATEST(next_id, floor)`, which X-locks the sequence row and serializes concurrent callers), reads
    `next_id` `FOR UPDATE`, advances it and records the range. A failed range insert is logged and ignored unless it is
    a deadlock (1213, the whole transaction was rolled back) or a lost connection; those, like any other failure,
    retry the reservation (3 attempts, each on a checked connection, a dead one replaced).
  - Commits on its own: inside `transaction()` it raises `UnsupportedOperation` on every backend.
- **`select(table: Table, data: tuple[SafeDataType, ...]) -> tuple[SafeDataType, ...] | None`**
  - Executes single-row query matching non-None column filters (`SELECT * FROM table WHERE ... LIMIT 1`). None
    positions act as wildcards.
- **`select_preload(table: Table, cached_columns: tuple[int, ...] | None = None, min_vid: int | None = None)
  -> list[tuple[SafeDataType, ...]]`**
  - Queries records for TableEngine startup preloading with column projection (e.g. `SELECT hash, ast_id FROM
    m_ast_hash`) and version filtering on the table's version column (`WHERE vid >= min_vid`, `WHERE (vid_e =
    0 OR vid_e >= min_vid)`, or `WHERE commit_id >= min_vid` for `m_bridge_checkpoint`). `min_vid` is a commit
    id (`gp.Old_VID`), so tables without a version column are never filtered (blob ids are a different id
    space).

- **`select_in(table: Table, col_idx: int, values: Sequence[SafeDataType]) -> list[tuple[SafeDataType,
  ...]]`**
  - Every row whose column `col_idx` is one of `values` (`MariaDB`: `IN` queries of 1000 values; `SQLiteDB` / `MockDB`:
    chunked `IN` queries; base default: one `view_select_multiple()` per value). Used to load the stored symbol items of a
    file's previous tags.

- **`table_size(table: Table, cached_columns: tuple[int, ...] | None = None, min_vid: int | None = None) ->
  int`**
  - Size of the table in bytes. `MariaDB` reads `DATA_LENGTH + INDEX_LENGTH` and `TABLE_ROWS` from
    `information_schema.TABLES` (InnoDB statistics, so an estimate) and returns 0 for a table that is not in
    the catalog; `SQLiteDB` / `MockDB` read the stored bytes from `dbstat` (0 when it is not compiled in).
  - With `cached_columns` narrower than the table, returns the share those columns are estimated to take
    (`estimate_column_bytes()` per row, capped by the table's own size).
  - With `min_vid`, returns the size of the rows `select_preload()` would return for it, so a version-scoped
    table is sized by its working window and not by its whole history. `MariaDB` counts that window with the
    same version predicate `select_preload()` uses (`_version_predicate()`, an index range scan over the rows
    the caller is about to read anyway) and scales the catalog size to it; the table's bytes and total row
    count are never scanned.
  - The base implementation returns 0, meaning the size is unknown: `TECachedDB.cache_max_bytes` then caches
    the table as configured.
  - Used by `TECachedDB` to leave a cached table above `cache_max_bytes` (`parser.cache_max_table_mb`) out of
    the cache (`table_engine/TE_API.md` §2.2).

### 2.3. Multi-Table Relational Views
- **`view_select(tables: Sequence[Table] | dict[int, Table], joins: JoinsType, columns: tuple[SafeDataType,
  ...]) -> tuple[SafeDataType, ...] | None`**
  - Executes joined single-row query across relational join graph (`JoinsType`) matching non-None column
    filters.
- **`view_select_multiple(tables: Sequence[Table] | dict[int, Table], joins: JoinsType, columns:
  tuple[SafeDataType, ...]) -> list[tuple[SafeDataType, ...]]`**
  - Executes joined multi-row query across relational join graph (`JoinsType`) and fetches all matching rows.
  - **Large Graph Chunking**: Graphs exceeding 50 tables are chunked into slices of <= 30 tables per step.

### 2.4. Batch Insert, Upsert & Parallel Commits
- **`insert(table: Table, data: tuple[tuple[SafeDataType, ...], ...] | tuple[SafeDataType, ...]) -> None`**
  - Batch executes parameterized `INSERT INTO table VALUES (%s, ...)`. Dynamically sizes batches based on
    table schema: tables with `TEXT`, `LONGTEXT`, or `BLOB` columns (e.g. `m_ast_debug`) are capped at <= 500
    rows and <= 4MB estimated payload, while regular tables use <= 2000 rows (or <= 5000 rows for short
    tables) and <= 8MB. On `OperationalError 1153` (`ER_NET_PACKET_TOO_LARGE` / `max_allowed_packet`),
    recursively bisects chunks into halves until execution succeeds. On duplicate primary key collisions
    (MySQL `errno 1062` / `IntegrityError` in `MariaDB`, or a UNIQUE / PRIMARY KEY failure in `SQLiteDB` / `MockDB`), raises `ValueError` to
    preserve driver contract. Tables with `idempotent_pk=True` skip only the rows whose key already exists:
    `MariaDB` appends a no-op `ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE pk = pk` (`_insert_sql()`), since a plain multi-row
    INSERT fails as a whole on one duplicate and `INSERT IGNORE` would also downgrade every other error of the
    statement (truncated values, foreign-key failures) to a warning; `SQLiteDB` / `MockDB` skip existing keys.
    Outside `transaction()` each chunk is committed by autocommit; a chunk whose connection was lost is retried on
    a new connection (3 attempts) with the same no-op `ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE`, because the lost acknowledgement
    may belong to a chunk the server already committed (the TableEngine allocates the keys, so an existing key can
    only be that earlier write).
- **`update(table: Table, data: tuple[tuple[SafeDataType, ...], ...] | tuple[SafeDataType, ...]) -> None`**
  - Batch executes upsert `INSERT INTO table VALUES (...) ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE col=VALUES(col)` for all
    non-primary key columns. Uses dynamic byte-bounded chunking and recursive bisection on packet limit
    errors. Outside `transaction()` each chunk is committed by autocommit.
- **`commit_tables_parallel(tables_data: Sequence[tuple[Table, Sequence[tuple], Sequence[tuple]]],
  max_workers: int | None = None, dedicated: bool = False) -> list[TableCommitStat]`**
  - Flushes insert and update payloads across multiple tables concurrently using dedicated worker connection
    threads (`MariaDB`); a single table is written on the instance's own connection unless `dedicated=True`
    (set by the TableEngine's background writer thread, which must never touch the owner's connection).
  - Every table is written as one `transaction()` on both paths (the instance's own connection for a single
    table, a dedicated connection per table otherwise), so a failed table leaves nothing committed. A lost
    connection rolls that table back and it is written again (3 attempts, a dead connection replaced); other errors
    are not retried. The later attempts insert with `ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE pk = pk`: when only the COMMIT
    acknowledgement was lost the earlier attempt is committed, and its rows are skipped instead of failing with a
    duplicate key.
  - Every table runs to completion; if any failed, the first error is raised with `failed_table_ids` (the
    tables that were not committed; all others were). `SQLiteDB` / `MockDB` write tables one after the other and name the
    failing table and the ones after it.
  - Returns one `TableCommitStat(table_name, inserted, updated, seconds)` per written table (exported by
    `db_engine`).
  - `supports_background_commit` (class attribute, `True` for `MariaDB`) tells the TableEngine that
    `dedicated=True` keeps the call off the instance's connection, so it may run on a writer thread.

### 2.5. DDL & Index Management
- **`create_table(tables: Sequence[Table] | Table) -> None`**
  - Renders each table with `sql_render.render_create_table_statements(table, dialect)` from `table.init_columns`
    (neutral `(name, ColumnSpec)` pairs), `table.init_primary`, `table.unique_keys`, `table.indexes` and
    `table.init_foreign`, creates tables, inserts seed rows (`table.initial_insert`), and commits. MariaDB output is
    one `CREATE TABLE` statement per table with the keys inline (pinned byte for byte by `unit_test/test_ddl_render.py`);
    SQLite output is the table (an `auto_increment` column becomes `INTEGER ... PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT`, `UNSIGNED` is
    dropped, `BINARY(n)` is `BLOB`) plus one `CREATE INDEX` per secondary index. `render_create_table(table, dialect)`
    returns the first statement.
- **`drop_table(tables: Sequence[Table] | Table) -> None`**
  - Temporarily sets `SET FOREIGN_KEY_CHECKS = 0;`, drops tables via `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS`, and restores `SET
    FOREIGN_KEY_CHECKS = 1;`.
- **`create_view(view_name: str, select: Select | str, replace: bool = True) -> None`**
  - Creates or replaces a database view. A `Select` spec is rendered for the engine's dialect with its parameters inlined
    as literals (`render_select_literal()`; SQLite replaces via `DROP VIEW IF EXISTS` + `CREATE VIEW`); a SQL string is accepted
    for legacy callers only.
- **`drop_view(view_name: str, if_exists: bool = True) -> None`**
  - Drops a database view if present.
- **`add_column(table_name: str, column_name: str, spec: ColumnSpec) -> bool`**
  - Adds a neutrally described column (`ColumnSpec`, §2.6) when the table lacks it and returns whether it was added;
    each engine renders its own type (`render_column_ddl(name, spec, dialect)`). `MockDB` stores a NOT NULL column without a default as nullable and answers
    `column_info()` from the declared spec.
- **`add_column_if_missing(table_name: str, column_name: str, column_def: str) -> bool`**
  - Legacy form with a MariaDB DDL fragment: checks the catalog and executes `ALTER TABLE <table_name> ADD COLUMN <column_def>` if missing.
- **`index_exists(index_name: str, table: Table) -> bool`**
  - Queries `SHOW INDEX FROM table WHERE Key_name = %s`.
- **`create_index(index_name: str, table: Table, rows: tuple[PointerType, ...]) -> None`**
  - Creates single-column or composite index if not already present.
- **`remove_index(index_name: str, table: Table) -> None`**
  - Drops index if present via `ALTER TABLE table DROP INDEX index_name`.
- **`create_indexes(indexes: Sequence[tuple[str, Table, tuple[PointerType, ...]]], max_workers: int | None =
  None) -> None`**
  - Creates multiple database indexes in parallel across worker connections.
- **`remove_indexes(indexes: Sequence[tuple[str, Table]], max_workers: int | None = None) -> None`**
  - Removes multiple database indexes in parallel across worker connections.
- **`test_tables(tables: Sequence[Table] | Table) -> list[str] | None`**
  - Checks if all registered schema tables exist in the database catalog; returns list of missing table names
    or `None`.
- **`verify_relational_integrity(tables: Sequence[Table]) -> dict[str, int]`**
  - Verifies relational foreign key integrity across tables and returns any orphan record counts (empty
    dictionary if all constraints valid).

### 2.6. Declarative Query Specification Primitives (`db_engine/spec.py`)
Declarative AST types allowing callers across all subsystems to construct rich relational queries, filters, joins, and aggregates without writing raw SQL strings.

- **Data Types**:
  - `Source`: Table schema object, table/view name, or `(Table | name, alias)` tuple.
  - `Cond(op, value, value2)`: Parameterized operator term.
  - `Col(name)`: Explicit column reference (e.g. for compare-and-set or join terms).
  - `Value(v)`: Explicit literal scalar parameter.
  - `Inc(n)`: Atomic increment / decrement expression (`col = col + n`).
  - `Join(source, on, kind="inner"|"left", joins=())`: Relational join clause with nested join support.
  - `Agg(func, column="*", distinct=False)`: Aggregate function (`COUNT`, `SUM`, `MIN`, `MAX`, `AVG`).
  - `Const(value)`: Constant literal column projection.
  - `Select(source, columns, where=None, joins=(), distinct=False, order_by=(), limit=None, offset=None, group_by=(), having=None, hint=None)`: Pure select specification. `columns` items are a column name, `Agg`, `Const` or an expression; `order_by` / `group_by` items are a name (`"-col"` descending), an expression or `Order(expr, desc)`; `having` is a Where over aggregates (`Pred(Agg(...), cond)`) or output aliases; `hint="straight_join"` asks MariaDB to join in written order (other dialects ignore it). An `offset` without `limit` is honored.
  - `AnyOf(*branches)`: Disjunction (`OR`) combinator across condition branches.
  - `Exists(source, on, where=None, joins=(), negate=False)`: Correlated subquery existence test (`EXISTS` / `NOT EXISTS`).
  - `InSelect(columns, source, select, where=None, joins=(), negate=False)`: Set membership subquery (`col IN (SELECT ...)` or tuple `(a, b) IN (SELECT a, b ...)`).
  - `InQuery(columns, select)` / `in_select(columns, Select, negate=False)`: `col IN (SELECT ...)` and tuple `(a, b) IN (SELECT a, b ...)` over a full `Select` (joins, distinct, expressions).
  - `ExistsQuery(select)` / `exists_select(Select, negate=False)`: `[NOT] EXISTS (SELECT ...)`; a correlated select references outer columns with `Col("alias.col")` values.
  - `Pred(expr, test)`: Where term testing an expression; `test` is a `Cond` (`Pred(Length("name"), gt(3))`), an operand (equality), a scalar or `None` (`IS NULL`).
- **Expressions** (usable in select columns, `Pred`, `order_by` / `group_by`, `update_rows` values, `Join.on` values and Mapping where values `{col: expr}`):
  - Operand rule: a `str` is a column reference, `Value(v)` / `Const(v)` or any other scalar a bound literal, `Expr` / `Agg` a nested expression.
  - `Concat(*parts)` (`CONCAT` / `||`, NULL if any part is NULL), `Length(x)` (characters: `CHAR_LENGTH` on MariaDB, `LENGTH` on SQLite), `Substr(x, start, length=None)` (1-based; `Substr(x, 1, n)` is `LEFT(x, n)`), `Coalesce(*parts)`, `NullIf(a, b)`, `Hex(x)` (upper-case hex of a binary operand), `Arith(op, a, b)` with `add` / `sub` / `mul` helpers (`+ - *`; division is dialect-dependent and not offered), `Case([(where, value), ...], otherwise=None)` (each `where` is any Where; `Pred` tests expressions; a string result is a column name, a text literal is `Value("text")`), `Incoming(column)` (the value a conditional upsert offered: `VALUES(col)` / `excluded.col`; legal only in `insert_rows(update_exprs=...)`).
  - `Order(expr, desc=False)`: ORDER BY / GROUP BY item over an expression.
- **Neutral column description**:
  - `ColumnType`: `INT, BIGINT, MEDIUMINT, SMALLINT, TINYINT, BOOL, TEXT, MEDIUMTEXT, LONGTEXT, CHAR, VARCHAR, BINARY, VARBINARY, BLOB, MEDIUMBLOB, LONGBLOB, DATETIME, TIMESTAMP, FLOAT, DOUBLE, JSON`.
  - `ColumnSpec(type, length=None, unsigned=False, nullable=True, default=NO_DEFAULT, auto_increment=False, bin_collation=False, explicit_null=False)`: `length` is required for `CHAR` / `VARCHAR` / `BINARY` / `VARBINARY`; `default` is `NO_DEFAULT` (no clause), `None` (`DEFAULT NULL`), `CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` or a literal; `bin_collation` asks for case-sensitive text (`COLLATE utf8mb4_bin` on MariaDB, a no-op on SQLite); `explicit_null` spells `NULL` out in MariaDB DDL (cosmetic). Properties `is_binary`, `is_large`, `is_integer`. `render_column_ddl(name, spec, dialect)` renders MariaDB DDL (`TINYINT(1)` for `BOOL`, `UNSIGNED`, `AUTO_INCREMENT`) or SQLite DDL (integer types become `INTEGER`, text-like types `TEXT`, binary types `BLOB`, floating types `REAL`, `auto_increment` becomes `PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT`).
  - Schema constructors (`INT(...)`, `BIGINT`, `MEDIUMINT`, `SMALLINT`, `TINYINT`, `CHAR(n)`, `VARCHAR(n)`, `TEXT`, `MEDIUMTEXT`, `BIN(n)`, `MEDIUMBLOB`) build a `ColumnSpec` NOT NULL by default (`unsigned=`, `null=True|None`, `default=`, `auto=`, `bin_collation=`); `core/DBLayout.py` is written with them. `as_column_spec(...)` / `parse_column_fragment(...)` convert legacy DDL fragments (`("INT", "NOT NULL")`) for ad-hoc `Table(...)` definitions.
- **Where forms**: a mapping `{column: value}` ANDs its entries; a list of terms ANDs them; `AnyOf` ORs branches. A mapping value is:
  - a scalar: `column = value`; `None`: `column IS NULL` (on every backend; `is_null()` is the same); `Col(other)` / an expression: `column = <expr>`;
  - a list / tuple / set: `column IN (...)`. **An empty list matches nothing** (SQL semantics; `update_rows` / `delete_rows` / `select_rows` return 0 / `[]` without a round trip). A `None` inside an IN list never matches (SQL semantics);
  - a `Cond`: one condition; a **list of `Cond`s**: all of them ANDed, which puts several conditions on one column: `{"a": [ge(1), lt(10), ne(5)]}`. A list mixing conditions and plain values, or a mapping as the value, raises `SpecError`;
  - `all_of(*terms)` (AND, flattens lists) and `any_of(*terms)` (OR, same as `AnyOf`) combine whole terms: `all_of({"a": ge(1)}, {"a": lt(10)}, any_of({"b": 1}, {"b": 2}))`.
  - `Join.on` / `Exists.on` values follow the same `None` rule (`IS NULL`).
- **NULL handling**: `eq(None)` is `IS NULL` and `ne(None)` is `IS NOT NULL`; `lt` / `le` / `gt` / `ge` / `between` / `ieq` with `None` raise `SpecError` (comparing with NULL never matches). `ne(v)` and `not_in(...)` never match a NULL column value on any backend.
- **Aliases**: `render_select` (hence every engine) validates every `alias.column` reference of the columns, joins, where, having, group_by and order_by against the aliases (or unaliased table names) of the select's source and joins; subqueries (`exists_select`, `in_select`, `Exists`, `finished_ref("r")`) may also use the aliases of every enclosing select. An unknown alias raises `SpecError` listing the known aliases, so `finished_ref("r")` inside a select aliased `bc` fails at build time instead of returning wrong rows.
- **Condition Helpers**:
  - `eq(v)`: `col = v` (needed to combine an equality with other conditions on one column); `ne(v)`, `lt(v)`, `le(v)`, `gt(v)`, `ge(v)`: Standard scalar comparisons (`<>`, `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`).
  - `between(lo, hi)`: Range inclusion (`BETWEEN lo AND hi`).
  - `not_in(seq)`: Negated set membership (`NOT IN (...)`).
  - `is_null()`, `not_null()`: Nullity predicates (`IS NULL`, `IS NOT NULL`).
  - `like(text, mode="prefix"|"suffix"|"contains"|"exact", ci=False)`: Pattern matching with automatic wildcard escaping and dialect-specific `ESCAPE` clauses.
  - `ieq(v)`: Case-insensitive equality (`LOWER(col) = LOWER(%s)`).
  - `hash_prefix(prefix_bytes)`: Binary hash prefix range scan (`col >= lo AND col < hi`).
  - `len_lt(n)`: Column string length check (`LENGTH(col) < n`).
  - `finished_ref(alias="r")`: Subquery checking absence of active `INGEST_PARSING` tasks.
- **Query Optimization Helpers**:
  - `has_empty_in_term(where)`: Introspects where terms; short-circuits empty queries to `[]` without network round trips.
  - `find_oversize_in_term(where, chunk_size=1000)`: Detects IN clauses exceeding threshold for automatic batch chunking.
  - `replace_in_term(where, term_idx, target_col, sub_list)`: Clones query specification substituting chunked IN terms.
  - `dedup_rows(rows, as_dict)`: Preserves distinct result order across chunked multi-pass queries.

### 2.7. Spec Read Primitives
Common query primitives implemented across `BaseDBEngine`, `MariaDB`, `MockDB`, `ReadSession`, and (independently of `BaseDBEngine`) `SQLiteStore`.

- **`select_rows(source, columns, where=None, *, joins=(), distinct=False, order_by=(), limit=None, offset=None, as_dict=None, group_by=(), having=None, hint=None) -> list[tuple | dict]`**
  - Executes declarative select query. Honors auto-chunking for oversize IN lists (> 1000 items in MariaDB / 500 in SQLite; not for grouped reads) and returns empty lists immediately for empty IN clauses. Defaults to tuples on drivers and dicts on `ReadSession`. `MariaDB` returns `bytes` for every BINARY / VARBINARY / BLOB column it projects as a plain column (schema-aware; mysql-connector sometimes decodes valid-UTF-8 binary values to `str`), likewise `select()`, `select_in()`, `select_preload()`, `view_select*()`. Ordering treats NULL as the smallest value on every engine.
- **`select_spec(select: Select, *, as_dict=None) -> list[tuple | dict]`**
  - Runs a complete `Select` object through `select_rows()` (also on `ReadSession`).
- **`iter_rows(source, columns, where=None, *, joins=(), distinct=False, order_by=(), limit=None, offset=None, as_dict=None, chunk_size=2000) -> Iterator[tuple | dict]`**
  - Streaming iterator over query results yielding rows in chunks.
- **`select_one(source, columns, where=None, *, joins=(), order_by=(), as_dict=None) -> tuple | dict | None`**
  - Fetches the first matching row or returns `None`.
- **`select_values(source, column, where=None, *, joins=(), distinct=False, order_by=(), limit=None, offset=None) -> list[Any]`**
  - Returns a flat list of scalar values for a single projected column.
- **`select_value(source, column, where=None, default=None, *, joins=(), order_by=()) -> Any`**
  - Returns a single scalar value from the first matching row, or `default` if no rows match.
- **`count_rows(source, where=None, *, joins=()) -> int`**
  - Executes `COUNT(*)` query matching specification filters.
- **`row_exists(source, where=None, *, joins=()) -> bool`**
  - Executes optimized `SELECT 1 ... LIMIT 1` existence probe.
- **`min_value(source, column, where=None, *, joins=()) -> Any`**
  - Computes `MIN(column)` over filtered relation.
- **`max_value(source, column, where=None, *, joins=()) -> Any`**
  - Computes `MAX(column)` over filtered relation.
- **`aggregate(source, aggs, where=None, *, joins=(), group_by=(), order_by=(), as_dict=None, having=None) -> list[tuple | dict]`**
  - Computes dictionary of aggregate expressions (`Agg`) with `GROUP BY group_by [HAVING having]`; the group columns are returned first, keyed by their base name.
- **`resolve_relation_name(relation: Source) -> str`**
  - Canonical identifier resolution stripping aliases or prefix qualifications.

### 2.8. Spec Write Primitives
Typed write methods eliminating raw caller SQL during data modification and task queue coordination.

- **`insert_rows(table, columns, rows, *, on_conflict="error"|"ignore"|"update"|"replace", update_columns=None, chunk_size=None, update_exprs=None) -> int`**
  - Inserts batch of rows. A column left out of `columns` takes its declared default on every backend. Resolves conflict semantics across MariaDB and SQLite (`ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE` / `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE`). Under a packet-size error on MariaDB, recursively bisects chunks. `on_conflict="error"` raises `DuplicateKeyError`. Returns the rows written (see **Affected-row counts**).
  - **Conditional upsert**: `on_conflict="update"` assigns the incoming value to `update_columns` (default: every inserted column, or none when `update_exprs` is given) and evaluates `update_exprs: {column: Expr}` for the others. `Incoming("col")` is the offered value, a bare column name the stored value, `Case([...], otherwise)` makes an assignment conditional, e.g. `{"commit_id": Case([(Pred(Incoming("commit_id"), gt(0)), Incoming("commit_id"))], "commit_id")}` for `IF(VALUES(commit_id) > 0, VALUES(commit_id), commit_id)`.
  - **Assignment semantics (all backends)**: every expression of `update_exprs` and of `update_rows(values=...)` reads the STORED (pre-update) row, whatever the order the mapping is written in; `Incoming("col")` reads the offered value. MariaDB evaluates `SET` / `ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE` left to right on the already-updated row, so its renderer reorders the assignments (a stable topological order: an assignment that reads column B precedes the assignment of B; the written order is kept where it already works). Assignments that read each other (`a = b + 1, b = a + 1`) have no such order and raise `SpecError` on every backend; split them into two statements.
- **`get_or_insert_id(table, key, values=None) -> int`**
  - Fetches existing primary key matching `key`, or inserts a new row with `key` and `values` combined and returns the generated sequence ID.
- **`update_rows(table, values, where=None, *, limit=None) -> int`**
  - Updates rows matching filter. Supports atomic expressions (`Inc`, `Col`, any `Expr`, all reading the stored row). Auto-chunks oversize IN lists (> 1000 items). Returns the rows matched, also those whose values do not change.
- **`delete_rows(table, where=None, *, limit=None, all_rows=False) -> int`**
  - Deletes rows matching filter. Requires `all_rows=True` when `where=None` to prevent accidental table wipes. Auto-chunks oversize IN lists. `limit` renders `DELETE ... LIMIT n` on MariaDB and `DELETE ... WHERE rowid IN (SELECT rowid ... LIMIT n)` on SQLite (the same for `update_rows(limit=)`). Returns the rows deleted.
- **`copy_rows(target_table, columns, select, *, on_conflict="error"|"ignore") -> int`**
  - Performs server-side `INSERT INTO target (cols) SELECT ...` data migration without round-tripping rows through client memory. The `Select` may join, be `distinct`, project expressions (`Concat`, `Substr`, `Case`, `Const`) and carry `hint="straight_join"` (MariaDB only); `on_conflict="ignore"` renders `INSERT IGNORE` / `INSERT OR IGNORE`. Returns the rows inserted.
- **Affected-row counts** (one meaning on every backend): `insert_rows` with `error` / `ignore` and `copy_rows` count the rows inserted (an ignored duplicate counts 0); `insert_rows` with `update` / `replace` counts every offered row once (inserted, updated or replaced, also when the stored values stay the same; never 2 per row); `update_rows` counts the rows matched; `delete_rows` the rows deleted. Compare-and-set claims (`update_rows(..., {"status": ELIGIBLE})` returning 1 for the single winner, 0 for the others) rely on this. MariaDB connects with `CLIENT_FOUND_ROWS` and `insert_rows` returns the batch size for `update` / `replace`.

### 2.9. Catalog & Server Introspection
Introspection primitives exposing database metadata and runtime configuration.

- **`existing_tables(candidates: Sequence[str]) -> set[str]`**
  - Queries database catalog for existence of specified table names.
- **`table_exists(table_name: str) -> bool`**, **`create_view(...)`**, **`drop_view(...)`**, **`add_column_if_missing(...)`**
  - `BaseDBEngine` defaults issue `information_schema` / DDL SQL through `_raw_query()` / `_raw_execute()`. `SQLiteDB` / `MockDB` answer from `sqlite_master` / `PRAGMA`; `MockDB` also reports a `core/DBLayout.py` table that was not dropped (and, with `include_views`, a registry view) as existing before its first use creates it.
- **`column_exists(table: Table | str, column: str) -> bool`**
  - Checks if a specific column exists in the database table schema.
- **`column_info(table: Table | str, column: str) -> ColumnInfo | None`**
  - Returns `ColumnInfo(data_type, column_type, octet_length, nullable)`; `octet_length` is `CHARACTER_OCTET_LENGTH` (the byte width of a `BINARY(n)` column is `n`; `MockDB` derives it from the schema).
- **`table_stats(tables: Sequence[Table | str]) -> list[TableStats]`**
  - Returns list of `TableStats(table_name, row_count, data_bytes, index_bytes)`.
- **`server_variable(name: str) -> str | None`**
  - Introspects global server configuration parameter (`None` when the engine has no such variable).

### 2.10. Schema Maintenance & View Registry (`db_engine/views.py`)
- **`drop_tables(names: Sequence[str], *, ignore_fk: bool = False, if_exists: bool = True) -> None`**
  - Drops multiple tables by name (`render_drop_tables()`: one statement on MariaDB, one per table on SQLite). `ignore_fk=True` suspends foreign-key checks for the drop and restores the session's previous setting.
- **`ensure_columns(table: Table, columns: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> list[str]`**
  - Reflects table schema against database catalog and adds missing columns via `ALTER TABLE`.
- **`ensure_views(views: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> None`**
  - Creates or replaces views registered in `ORDERED_VIEW_NAMES` in topological dependency order.
- **View SQL helpers** (`db_engine/views.py`): `TREE_VIEW_SQL`, `SYMBOL_VIEW_SQL` (read by `ensure_views()`) hold the only SQL text of those views; callers outside `db_engine/` use `ensure_views()` and the engine's `symbol_refs_of_targets()` / `symbol_def_blobs_of_targets()` (§2.11). The `m_symbol_own.kind` constants `KIND_REFS = 1` / `KIND_DEFS = 2` are shared with `core/SymbolRows.py`.
- **Canonical Views**:
  - `m_v_main`: Canonical release tags view.
  - `m_checkpoint_tree`: Milestone checkpoint tree synthesis.
  - `m_bridge_file`: Active file bridge pointer.
  - `m_file`: Unique file blob registry.
  - `m_bridge_commit_file`: Commit to file bridge relations.
  - `m_symbol_def`: Symbol definitions with bit-packed identifier flags.
  - `m_symbol_ref`: Symbol references.

### 2.11. Pipeline Intent Methods
Specialized high-level database operations driving parser pipeline workers.

- **`new_checkpoint_pairs(commit_id: int, prev_commit_id: int) -> Iterator[NewPairs]`**
  - Context manager yielding a `NewPairs` for the `(fnid, blob_id)` pairs of `commit_id`'s checkpoint that `prev_commit_id`'s lacks: `pairs: set[tuple[int, int]]`, `delete_rows_of(table) -> int` (rows whose `(source_blob_id, source_fnid)` is a new pair) and `insert_include_references(kconfig_type_ids, kconfig_ref_type, include_ref_type) -> int` (`m_file_reference` rows of the new pairs' `#include` / Kconfig source tags, `INSERT IGNORE`-style). The base implementation `SpecNewPairs` (`db_engine/base.py`, used by `MockDB` and `SQLiteDB`) holds no connection-local state: the deletes use `in_select`, the copy is one `copy_rows(Select(..., hint="straight_join", distinct=True))` with `Case` / `Substr`. `MariaDB` overrides it with a connection-local temporary table (`tmp_new_pairs`) for speed and falls back to the inline anti-join when the table cannot be created.
- **`enqueue_parse_tasks(rows: Sequence[Sequence[Any]]) -> int`**
  - Publishes `(network_id, chain_name, chain_kind, seq_order, ref_name, commit_id, base_ref_name, base_commit_id, status)` rows to `m_parse_task` (identity `(network_id, ref_name)`) as one chunked multi-row `insert_rows(on_conflict="update", update_exprs=...)` inside one transaction; returns how many rows were written (every offered row). Rows are applied in order, each against the row stored so far, so a task listed twice ends as if published twice and the result equals one call per row. The status the row already has decides what is kept: a FAILED task, or a DONE one published as not done, starts over (published status, `retry_count` 0, `error_msg` cleared); a LEASED / RECLAIMING task keeps its state unless published as DONE; any other takes the published status. A known `commit_id` / `base_commit_id` is never replaced by 0. `retry_count` / `error_msg` precede `status` in the assignments, so they read the stored status on MariaDB's left-to-right evaluation as well as on SQLite and `MockDB`. Implemented once in `BaseDBEngine`.
- **`record_task_failure(task_id: int, error_msg: str, *, worker_id: str | None = None, max_attempts: int = 3) -> int`**
  - One conditional `update_rows` on a LEASED / RECLAIMING task (of `worker_id` when given): `status` becomes FAILED when `retry_count + 1 >= max_attempts`, else ELIGIBLE (assigned before `retry_count` is incremented, reading the stored count), `error_msg` is cut to 1000 characters, `worker_id` cleared. Returns the rows changed (0: not leased or not this worker's). Implemented once in `BaseDBEngine`.
- **`next_eligible_parse_tasks(network_id: int, status: int, *, limit: int = 10) -> list[tuple]`**
  - `(task_id, chain_name, chain_kind, ref_name, commit_id, base_ref_name, base_commit_id)` of the tasks of `status`: stable chains first, then shorter then alphabetical chain names, by `seq_order`. Implemented once in `BaseDBEngine`.
- **`symbol_refs_of_targets(ast_ids, *, role=None, with_caller=False, limit=None) -> list[dict]`** / **`symbol_def_blobs_of_targets(ast_ids) -> set[tuple[int, int]]`**
  - References (`role, line, char_s, fid, tag_id, ast_id` + `caller`) and definition `(ast_id, blob_id)` pairs of target ASTs, read key first (`m_blob_symbol.target_ast_id` -> shared `m_tag_ref` / `m_tag_def` rows through their placements, skipping placements marked in `m_symbol_own`, plus the per-blob rows) with query specs in `db_engine/symbol_rows.py` (`symbol_refs_of_targets(reader, ...)`, `symbol_def_blobs_of_targets(reader, ...)` take anything with `select_rows`). Implemented once in `BaseDBEngine`, and through `ReadIntents` on every read session (§2.12).

### 2.12. Webapp Read Session & Query Primitives (`db_engine/pool.py`)
Read-only query abstraction for web services providing dictionary-mapped results and specialized intent methods.

- **Pool configuration**:
  - `configure_pool(config_provider: Callable[[], dict] | dict) -> None` injects the `database` configuration section
    (a callable is re-evaluated each time the pool is built, so a started SSH tunnel's rewritten host/port is seen).
    `db_engine` never imports `webapp`; `webapp/backend/database/pool.py` calls
    `configure_pool(get_backend_db_config)` at import.
  - Building the pool raises `PoolConfigError` when no configuration was injected or `user` / `password` is missing;
    there is no credential fallback.

- **Acquisition & lifecycle**:
  - `Engine.reader() -> ContextManager[ReadSession]` (class-level; `get_db_reader()` is the `MariaDB` implementation), `Engine.warm_up()`, `Engine.shutdown()` (§2.1).
  - Catalog pass-throughs on every read session (`ReadSession`, `MockReadSession`, `SQLiteReadSession`): `table_stats`, `column_exists`, `column_info`, `index_names`, `existing_tables`, `resolve_relation_name`, plus `select_spec` and `close`.
  - Read-only enforcement: write and DDL entry points of the spec API (`execute`, `insert_rows`, `update_rows`, `delete_rows`, `copy_rows`, `drop_tables`, `create_view`, `add_column`, ...) raise `ReadOnlyViolation`. The MariaDB session's connection and cursor are private; no raw-cursor leasing API exists, so every read path of the webapp is guarded (`unit_test/test_db_contract.py`, `tests/test_webapp_system.py`).
- **Catalog caching** (`ReadSession`): `resolve_relation_name`, `column_exists` and `index_names` answers are remembered on the pool (process-wide): a positive `column_exists` and `resolve_relation_name("m_checkpoint_tree") == "m_checkpoint_tree"` for the pool's lifetime, any other answer for 5 minutes (a database migrated while the webapp runs). Services therefore call them per request instead of keeping module-level schema flags.
- **Domain Intent Methods** (`db_engine/read_intents.py`, class `ReadIntents`): implemented once over query specs and inherited by `ReadSession`, `MockReadSession` and `SQLiteReadSession` (one implementation, same results on every backend); rows are dicts.
  - `list_network_commits(network_id, *, hash_prefix=None, text=None, authored_before=None, id_min=None, id_min_exclusive=False, id_max=None, newest_first=True, limit=50, offset=0) -> list[dict]`: `commit_id, commit_hash, author_date, subject, author_id, author_name, author_email, files_count` (the file counts come from one grouped read of `m_commit_file`).
  - `maintainer_sections(sec_ids=None, *, sec_id=None, name=None, member_person_ids=None, text=None, limit=None) -> list[dict]`: newest section first; the extended columns (`patchwork`, `bug_url`, `chat_channel`, `profile_doc`) are read when the database has them and are `None` otherwise; an empty `sec_ids` / `member_person_ids` list matches nothing.
  - `maintainer_developer_directory(sec_ids=None, credit_ids=None) -> list[dict]`: one profile per registered person (`subsystems_count, is_maintainer, is_reviewer, in_credits, has_commits`); an empty `sec_ids` / `credit_ids` list counts none of them.
  - `find_maintainer_person(raw, stripped, email, name) -> dict | None`: by id, e-mail or name, case-insensitive, a named person before an unnamed one, then the lowest id.
  - `symbol_name_page(prefix, *, after=None, limit=400) -> list[str]`: distinct names (`m_tag_def`, `m_blob_symbol_def`) shortest first, keyset paged after `(len(name), name)`.
  - `symbol_refs_of_targets(ast_ids, *, role=None, with_caller=False, limit=None)` / `symbol_def_blobs_of_targets(ast_ids)`: the key-first readers of `db_engine/symbol_rows.py` (§2.11).
  - **Checkpoint tree** (a version's full file tree is the `m_checkpoint_tree` view, or `m_bridge_checkpoint` on a database created before it): `checkpoint_tree_source() -> str` (the relation to use as a `Select` / `Join` source, e.g. `(reader.checkpoint_tree_source(), "bc")`; `resolve_relation_name("m_checkpoint_tree")`), `checkpoint_tree_exists(commit_id) -> bool`, `checkpoint_tree_files(commit_id, *, fnames=None, name=None, files_only=False, with_ftype=False, include_unnamed=False, order_by_name=False, limit=None) -> list[dict]` (`fnid, fname, blob_id[, ftype]`; `name` is a `Cond` such as `like(prefix, "prefix")`; `include_unnamed` left-joins `m_file_name`), `checkpoint_find_file(commit_id, candidates, suffix=None) -> str | None` (exact candidate names in order, else a path ending with `suffix`, shortest first; directories skipped). Services never rewrite table names in SQL text.

### 2.13. Embedded SQLite Store (`db_engine/sqlite_store.py`)
Standalone embedded SQLite store for local indexes, caches, and offline testing. `SQLiteStore` does not subclass `BaseDBEngine`; it mirrors a subset of the spec read/write primitives with its own signatures.

- **Features**:
  - WAL journaling mode with automatic checkpoints on transaction commit.
  - Thread-safe connection cache keyed by thread ID with `isolation_level=None`.
  - Schema management: `create_tables(specs)`, `drop_tables(names)`, `existing_tables(names)`, `column_exists(table, col)`.
  - Key-value metadata storage: `meta_get(key, default=None)` and `meta_set(key, value)`.
  - Multi-database attachment: `session(attach={"alias": "path"})`.
  - Automatic 500-item IN list batch chunking on reads and writes.
  - Declarative spec read and write execution (`select_rows`, `iter_rows`, `insert_rows`, `update_rows`, `delete_rows`, `clear`).

### 2.14. Foreign SQLite Reader (`db_engine/foreign.py`)
Read-only access to SQLite files written by other programs (for example public-inbox `over.sqlite3`).

- **`create_foreign_sqlite(path) -> ForeignWriter`** (fixtures and tools): `create_table(name, {column: ColumnSpec}, *, primary=())`, `insert_rows(table, columns, rows)` (each call commits), `close()`; builds a file `open_foreign_sqlite` can read.
- **`open_foreign_sqlite(path, *, readonly=True, immutable=True, timeout=60.0, cache_kib=8000) -> ForeignReader`**
  - Opens `file:<path>?mode=ro&immutable=1` (one lazily created connection per calling thread) and applies `PRAGMA busy_timeout`, `query_only = ON`, `cache_size = -<cache_kib>` and `temp_store = FILE`. A missing or unopenable file raises `ConnectionLostError`.
- **`ForeignReader`**: `select_rows`, `select_spec`, `iter_rows(..., chunk_size=2000)`, `select_one`, `select_values`, `select_value`, `count_rows`, `row_exists`, `aggregate`, `min_value`, `max_value`, `table_exists(name)`, `close_thread()` (closes the calling thread's connection), `close()` (every connection) and context-manager use. All reads are spec reads rendered with `dialect="sqlite"` (tuple rows by default, `as_dict=True` for dicts), so expressions (`Hex`, `Length`, ...), `group_by` and joins work; a missing table raises `MissingTableError`; lock/busy errors are retried 5 times with exponential backoff; other SQLite errors raise `DBError`.

### 2.15. SQLiteDB (`db_engine/sqlite_db.py`)

`SQLiteDB(path=None, *, read_only=False, foreign_keys=True, timeout=30.0)` is a full `BaseDBEngine`: every abstract and
spec method (TableEngine reads and writes, `select_rows` / `insert_rows` (all `on_conflict` modes, `update_columns`,
`update_exprs`) / `update_rows` / `delete_rows(limit=)` / `copy_rows`, `transaction()`, DDL and index management,
catalog introspection, `new_checkpoint_pairs`, `enqueue_parse_tasks`, `record_task_failure`,
`next_eligible_parse_tasks`, `reserve_id_block`, `commit_tables_parallel`) is implemented, and the base-class helpers
(`get_or_insert_id`, `ensure_columns`, `ensure_views`, `create_view`, `add_column`, `resolve_relation_name`) work through it.

- **Configuration**: `database.engine: "sqlite"` and `database.path` (exported as `DB_PATH`). Without `path` the file is
  `database.database` when that names a file (suffix `.db` / `.sqlite` / `.sqlite3` / path separator);
  with neither it is `":memory:"`; a bare schema name raises `ValueError` (no file is created implicitly in the working directory). `sqlite_path_from_config(cfg=None)` resolves it. `":memory:"` is private to one instance;
  `":memory:shared"` is a named shared-cache in-memory database several instances see. `--db sqlite` selects it on the CLI.
- **Connection model**: one connection per instance, `isolation_level=None` (autocommit unless `transaction()` holds a
  `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`), serialized by an `RLock`; file databases use WAL (`synchronous=NORMAL`), `busy_timeout`,
  `case_sensitive_like=ON` (matches `utf8mb4_bin` columns) and `foreign_keys=ON`. Nested `transaction()` blocks join the
  outermost one; `commit()` / `rollback()` inside it end the transaction and start the next.
- **Reader**: `db.reader()` returns a `SQLiteReadSession` (dict rows by default; select / aggregate / catalog calls;
  every write raises `ReadOnlyViolation`) over a fresh `mode=ro` + `query_only` connection of the same file (the instance
  itself for an in-memory database). `SQLiteDB.reader()` on the class uses a process-wide read-only connection to the
  configured path (`warm_up()` opens it, `shutdown()` closes it; a private `:memory:` database has none).
- **Capabilities**: `persistent` for files only; no `server_tuning`, `background_commit` or
  `concurrent_connections` (SQLite serializes writers). `probe_connection(cfg)` reports the SQLite version and never creates the file.
- **Errors**: `translate_sqlite_error(exc)`: UNIQUE / PRIMARY KEY violation -> `DuplicateKeyError`, "no such table" ->
  `MissingTableError`, "too many SQL variables" -> `PacketTooLargeError`, read-only database -> `ReadOnlyViolation`,
  closed / unreadable database -> `ConnectionLostError`; anything else is a `DBError`.
- **Backend differences** (everything else is behind the contract in `unit_test/test_db_contract.py`): an upsert conflicts on any unique key, a legacy `update()` on primary key and unique keys alike; integer widths and `UNSIGNED` are not enforced; `BINARY(n)` is an unpadded BLOB; `view_select` joins above 64 tables are unsupported (MariaDB chunks at 50); `table_stats` bytes need the `dbstat` virtual table (0 when absent); legacy raw SQL must be SQLite-valid (`%s` placeholders are rewritten to `?`); `hint="straight_join"` is ignored; registry views (`m_symbol_def`, ...) exist after `ensure_views()` and read the tables they join. Assignment order, NULL comparison, affected-row counts and alias validation are uniform and not listed here.

**MockDB** (`db_engine/mock_db.py`, `from db_engine import MockDB`; factory names `"mock"`, `"mockdb"`, `"inmemory"`)
is a `SQLiteDB` over an in-memory database, so a spec feature is implemented once per real dialect (MariaDB, SQLite) and
the mock evaluates it with SQLite, registry views and neutral errors included. `MockDB(use_global=True)` opens the
process-wide shared in-memory database (every such instance and `MockDB.reader()` on the class see it; `MockDB.reset()`
removes all its tables and views); `use_global=False` opens one private to the instance. `MockReadSession` is the
`SQLiteReadSession`. What differs from `SQLiteDB`:

- **Tables on first use**: a statement on a missing `core/DBLayout.py` table, a `Table` object that a call passed
  (`insert`, `select_rows(source)`, `create_table`, ...) or a registry view creates it from that schema; no initial rows
  except through `create_table()`. A table dropped with `drop_tables()` stays missing until `create_table()` /
  `create_view()`. `existing_tables()` / `table_exists()` report a non-dropped canonical table and (with `include_views`)
  a registry view as existing before their first use; `create_table()` keeps an existing table.
- **Lenient columns**: FOREIGN KEY constraints are not enforced and non-key columns accept NULL (a test inserts the columns it
  cares about); `column_info()` still reports the declared nullability, type and `octet_length`, and `add_column()` stores a
  NOT NULL column without a default as nullable.
- **Capabilities**: none (`persistent`, `server_tuning`, ...), `dialect` is `"sqlite"`; `close()` is a no-op (the database
  lives as long as the instance, or the process when shared) and `apply_server_tuning()` returns no notes.
- **No raw SQL**: `_raw_cursor` / `_raw_query*` / `_raw_execute*` / `_raw_delete` raise `UnsupportedOperation` when called
  directly; the engine's own helpers (view and column DDL) run them internally.
- **Test conveniences**: `MockDB.store` (class: the shared database; `db.store`: the instance) maps every non-empty table name to
  `{primary key: row tuple}` (`store.get(name, {})`, `store[name]` is `{}` for an unknown table, `items()`, `clear()` drops every
  table and view); `db.table_rows(name)` is the same for one table; `MockDB.reset()` clears the shared database.
  `tests/db_fixtures.py` (`make_db`, `patch_reader`, `DistDB`) is the one home of test database helpers.

The contract suite `unit_test/test_db_contract.py` runs one set of behavioural tests against `MockDB`, `SQLiteDB(":memory:")`
(the two are nearly identical; both stay in the suite to guard the `MockDB` wrapper)
and, with `KIP_CONTRACT_MARIADB=1` pointing at a scratch database (it drops and recreates a few `m_*` tables), `MariaDB`.

---

## 3. Factory Resolver (`get_db_engine`)

```python
from db_engine import get_db_engine

EngineClass = get_db_engine("mariadb")  # -> MariaDB (default)
EngineClass = get_db_engine("mock")     # -> MockDB
EngineClass = get_db_engine("sqlite")   # -> SQLiteDB
```

- `available_engines(*, include_aliases=False) -> tuple[str, ...]`: canonical engine names (`("mariadb", "mock", "sqlite")`), the list UIs and CLIs offer for `database.engine`.
- `register_engine(name, cls, aliases=())`: adds an engine to `get_db_engine()` / `available_engines()`.
- `default_socket_paths(name=None) -> tuple[str, ...]`: local server socket candidates of an engine (`MariaDB.default_socket_paths`).

| Engine Alias | Resolved Class | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `"mariadb"`, `"mysql"`, `None` | `MariaDB` | Production MySQL / MariaDB direct driver |
| `"mock"`, `"mockdb"`, `"inmemory"` | `MockDB` | In-memory mock database driver |
| `"sqlite"`, `"sqlite3"` | `SQLiteDB` | SQLite file / in-memory database driver (config below) |

---

## 4. Subsystem Verification & Regression Suite (`unit_test/test_db_engine.py`)

Comprehensive unit testing and contract verification across all database engines is implemented in
`unit_test/test_db_engine.py` using the reusable harness in `unit_test/harness.py`. Rendering of expressions,
grouping, subqueries, conditional upserts and column DDL for both dialects, `MockDB` specifics (tables on first use, raw SQL refusal, `store`),
neutral error mapping, capability flags, `probe_connection`, reader lifecycle / read-only guards, binary
normalization and the foreign SQLite reader are covered by `unit_test/test_db_spec_ext.py`.

Schema rendering is pinned by `unit_test/test_ddl_render.py` (the MariaDB `CREATE TABLE` text of every `core/DBLayout.py`
table against `unit_test/fixtures/mariadb_ddl_baseline.json`, byte for byte, plus SQLite DDL execution), and
`unit_test/test_db_contract.py` runs one behavioural contract against `MockDB`, `SQLiteDB(":memory:")` and (opt-in)
MariaDB (§2.15).

Key test capabilities:
- **Prefix Isolation**: Dynamically generates `t_*` test schemas from all tables in `core.DBLayout.TABLES`,
  rewriting foreign keys to eliminate collision with production `m_*` data.
- **Automated Cleanup & DB Reload**: Drops `t_*` tables at suite start and tearDown, and automatically reloads
  clean schemas upon test failure.
- **Dual Error Tracing**: On test failure, prints rich diagnostic reports featuring both feature-level error
  context and full Python tracebacks.
- **Dependency Propagation**: Enforces prerequisites (e.g. `depends_on=["insert"]`), automatically labeling
  downstream dependent tests as `UNTESTABLE` if prerequisite features fail.
- **Payload & Packet Resilience**: Tests handled recursive chunk bisection under `OperationalError 1153`
  (`max_allowed_packet`), verifies unhandled exception raising on oversized atomic rows, and exercises
  multi-megabyte byte-bounded chunking on live `LONGTEXT` columns.
